newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Britain's trade deficit shrinks in December.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Britain's trade deficit shrinks in December.

text.p: Britain's trade deficit with the rest of the world shrank to 845 million pounds ($1.38 billion) in December from 1.04 billion in November, official figures showed on Wednesday.
The figures were better than forecast and sterling recovered some ground against the mark in their wake. Government bonds also inched higher.

"The UK trade data are surprisingly good and do much to undermine recent complaints about a serious erosion of competitiveness due to sterling strength," said Jeremy Hawkins, economist at Bank of America.
The statistics office also announced it had harmonised its calculation of retail price rises to conform with European Union statistics. The new calculation showed inflation at 2.2 percent in January.

Figures released earlier this month showed January inflation at 2.8 percent. Core inflation, which excludes mortgage interest payments, was at 3.1 percent, well above the government target of 2.5 percent.
The inflation data are at the centre of a tussle between finance minister Kenneth Clarke and Bank of England governor Eddie George over whether interest rates should be raised.

Clarke, who wants rates held at 6.0 percent and says the recent strength of sterling will douse inflationary pressures, said on Wednesday Britain was a low inflation economy whatever calculation was used. ($1=.6107 Pound)
